The server API

Source: vignettes/server-api.Rmd
server-api.Rmd

Everything shadshiny does from the server falls into four groups: update input values, open/close overlays, raise toasts, and — for the few cases without a wrapper — send a custom message directly. All helpers are Shiny-module safe and default to the current reactive domain.

Updating inputs

Every valued component has an update_shad_*() twin taking the same inputId:

update_shad_select("plan", selected = "pro")
update_shad_combobox("lang", selected = c("R", "Python"), multiple = TRUE)
update_shad_checkbox("tos", value = TRUE)
update_shad_switch("dark", value = FALSE)
update_shad_radio_group("size", selected = "md")
update_shad_toggle("bold", value = TRUE)
update_shad_toggle_group("align", selected = "center")
update_shad_slider("volume", value = 60)
update_shad_input_otp("code", value = "123456")
update_shad_native_select("country", selected = "in")
update_shad_calendar("day", value = Sys.Date())
update_shad_date_picker("due", value = Sys.Date() + 7)
update_shad_tabs("tabs", selected = "billing")
update_shad_accordion("faq", value = "shipping")
update_shad_collapsible("details", open = TRUE)
update_shad_pagination("pager", selected = 2)
update_shad_carousel("gallery", selected = 3)
update_shad_resizable("split", sizes = c(35, 65))
update_shad_sidebar("shell", collapsed = TRUE)
update_shad_progress("upload", value = 80)
update_shad_button("save", loading = TRUE)         # or disabled=, label=
update_shad_command("palette", items = c("Recent: Q3.pdf" = "q3"))

Set or clear an error on the shad_form_field() wrapping a control directly:

update_shad_form_field("email", "Enter a valid email address.")
update_shad_form_field("email", NULL)

The one exception: text inputs. shad_input() and shad_textarea() render real <input>/<textarea> elements and use Shiny’s native text bindings. There is no update_shad_input(). Update them with base Shiny:

updateTextInput(session, "email", value = "you@example.com")
updateTextAreaInput(session, "bio", value = "Hello!")

Theming at runtime

update_shad_theme() swaps the preset and/or dark mode live:

observe(update_shad_theme(preset = input$preset, dark = input$dark))
update_shad_theme(preset = "default")     # clear the preset

Opening & closing overlays

Overlays can open from a UI trigger, or from the server by inputId:

shad_dialog_open("edit")          ; shad_dialog_close("edit")
shad_alert_dialog_open("confirm") ; shad_alert_dialog_close("confirm")
shad_sheet_open("filters")        ; shad_sheet_close("filters")
shad_drawer_open("cart")          ; shad_drawer_close("cart")
shad_popover_open("picker")       ; shad_popover_close("picker")
shad_sidebar_toggle("shell")      # collapse/expand the sidebar

A confirm flow with an alert-dialog:

observeEvent(input$delete, shad_alert_dialog_open("confirm_delete"))

observeEvent(input$confirm_delete, {      # the dialog's confirm action
  do_the_deletion()
  shad_alert_dialog_close("confirm_delete")
  shad_toast_success("Deleted.")
})

Overlays only reachable this way have to exist in the UI. When the content depends on what just happened, build the dialog in the server and show it — shiny::showModal()’s shape:

observeEvent(input$delete, {
  shad_show_dialog(shad_dialog(
    "confirm", title = paste("Delete", input$project, "?"),
    description = "This cannot be undone.",
    footer = tagList(shad_dialog_close_button(),
                     shad_button(inputId = "confirm_go", "Delete",
                                 variant = "destructive"))
  ))
})

It opens itself and, by default, destroys and removes itself once it closes — so inputs inside it are live while open and gone afterwards. Pass transient = FALSE to keep it (and its values) in the document for a later shad_dialog_open(). shad_remove_dialog(id) closes one from the server. Accepts shad_dialog(), shad_alert_dialog(), shad_sheet() and shad_drawer() — not shad_popover(), which has no trigger to anchor to.

Dialog and sheet content portals to <body> on open. The open element carries data-state="open" on .shad-dialog__content (not on the root #id). This matters if you probe open state from JavaScript — query the content globally, not as a descendant of the id.

Toasts

Toasts are entirely server-side. The base shad_toast() plus four shorthands:

shad_toast("Saved.")
shad_toast_success("Profile updated.")
shad_toast_error("Something went wrong.")
shad_toast_warning("Your trial ends in 3 days.")
shad_toast_loading("Uploading…")          # a persistent spinner toast

For a loading → done flow, capture the id and update it:

observeEvent(input$export, {
  id <- shad_toast_loading("Preparing export…")
  # ... do the work ...
  shad_toast_update(id, message = "Export ready.", type = "success")
})

shad_toast_dismiss(id)     # or shad_toast_dismiss() to clear all

Deferred callbacks run outside the reactive domain. If you raise or update a toast (or scroll a component) inside a later::later() / promises callback, the default-session lookup fails. Pass session explicitly, and wrap reactive reads/writes in shiny::withReactiveDomain(session, { ... }):

later::later(function() {
  shiny::withReactiveDomain(session, {
    shad_toast_update(id, message = "Done.", type = "success", session = session)
  })
}, delay = 2)

Binding an ExtendedTask to a button

bind_shad_task_button() is a presentation binding for an application-owned shiny::ExtendedTask. It observes task$status() and calls update_shad_button() for the four supported states:

Task status Button presentation
initial enabled, not loading
running loading, disabled, label_busy
success enabled, optional label_success
error enabled, optional label_error

The task still belongs to the application. The helper does not invoke it, call task$result(), create a worker, or choose an asynchronous backend. It returns the observer invisibly and destroys that observer when the session ends.

task <- shiny::ExtendedTask$new(function(value) {
  expensive_work(value)  # return a promise-compatible result
})

bind_shad_task_button(
  task, "run", label_busy = "Working...", label_success = "Complete",
  label_error = "Try again", session = session
)

observeEvent(input$run, task$invoke(input$value), ignoreInit = TRUE)

The async function can be supplied by an optional application dependency. Keep those choices outside shadshiny’s imports and guard them when writing reusable application examples:

if (requireNamespace("mirai", quietly = TRUE)) {
  task <- shiny::ExtendedTask$new(function(value) {
    mirai::mirai({ expensive_work(value) }, value = value)
  })
}

if (requireNamespace("promises", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE)) {
  task <- shiny::ExtendedTask$new(function(value) {
    promises::future_promise(expensive_work(value))
  })
}

These examples intentionally leave task creation, worker policy, error handling, and result rendering to the application. bind_shad_task_button() only translates the reactive lifecycle into button state.

The command palette from the server

shad_command_palette() opens on ⌘K, from shad_command_trigger(), or from the server:

shad_command_open("palette")
shad_command_close("palette")

# swap the items for whatever the session knows
update_shad_command("palette", items = list(
  "Recent" = c("Q3 report" = "q3", "Q4 forecast" = "q4")
))

Read selections from input$<id>_event, a list of value and nonce — not input$<id>:

observeEvent(input$palette_event, {
  switch(input$palette_event$value,
    dashboard = update_shad_tabs("nav", "dashboard"),
    reports   = update_shad_tabs("nav", "reports"))
})

input$<id> holds the last value, and Shiny drops a repeat of the same value. That is fine for a filter and wrong for navigation: choosing “Reports” twice has to work twice. _event fires every time.

The shadshiny:attr message sets or removes an attribute on any element — handy for, say, a password reveal that flips an input’s type:

observeEvent(input$reveal, {
  session$sendCustomMessage("shadshiny:attr",
    list(id = "password", attr = "type",
         value = if (revealed()) "text" else "password"))
})

Reading component values

Bound components report through input$<id> like any Shiny input. Two shapes are worth calling out:

  • Sidebar layout emits a list, not a scalar: input$shell is list(collapsed=, mobileOpen=, active=). Observe input$shell$active for the selected nav item.
  • Menus and command items report the chosen item’s value as an event — observe input$menu / input$cmd and switch on it.

Bookmarking

shadshiny inputs work with Shiny’s bookmarking. Turn it on with enableBookmarking("url") (or "server"). Components with a meaningful constructor initial value seed it through shiny::restoreInput(); the package’s strict, source-derived component-contract test keeps that set in sync as inputs evolve. This includes input OTP values and collapsible open state as well as the standard text, choice, date, navigation, and numeric controls.

Some state is intentionally not seeded from a single constructor value: transient overlay visibility; event-only menu, command, and navigation-menu activity; action-button counts and browser-security-constrained file uploads; and composite carousel, sidebar, resizable, or data-table state. Restore any application-specific version of that state explicitly in an onRestored() observer, using the component’s updater or imperative helper when one exists.

Gotchas checklist

  • No update_shad_input() — use updateTextInput() for shad_input().
  • Outputs inside an initially-hidden tab, dialog or sheet are suspended; set outputOptions(output, "id", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE).
  • Sidebar value is a list; watch $active.
  • In later/promises callbacks, pass session= and use withReactiveDomain().
  • shad_item(media = ) treats a string as an icon name. Pass "file" with media_variant = "icon", or wrap non-icon content in a tag — never a rendered shad_icon().
